newsitem.title: USA: James River debt shaken, rating news awaited.
newsitem.headline: James River debt shaken, rating news awaited.

text.p: James River Corp's bonds fell sharply after they became susceptible to downgrade when the company agreed to assume $2.4 billion of Fort Howard Corp debt in its merger propsal, traders and analysts said.
But analysts said benefits such as a successful history of debt reduction and promises of strong free cash flow by the two companies should ease management of the debt.

"Strategically, (the merger) makes a lot of sense," said Amy Eadon, fixed-income analyst at J.P. Morgan Securities. "Previously we've seen Kimberly Clark and Scott combine, and this gives James River much more of a platform and the ability to compete more effectively."

James River Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Miles Marsh and Fort Howard Chairman and CEO Michael Riordan reiterated a committment to using cash flow for debt reduction in an investor conference call on Monday morning. The companies estimated operating cash flow of more than $1.0 billion on a pro forma basis in 1996.

Still it remains that the assumption of $2.4 billion in high-couponed debt will jeopardize the James River credit ratings that sit just above junk status. James River senior debt is rated Baa3 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB-minus by Standard & Poor's.
Analysts and company executives noted that the rating agencies were not consulted on the planned merger.

Cindy Werneth, associate director at S&P, said the agency would look very favorably on the combined business position of the two companies. In addition, she said the promise of strong cash flows is of utmost importance in a review.
"Despite the high debt I think they are still going to have fairly healty cash flows, and we'll weigh that probably more than just the way the balance sheet looks per se," Werneth said.
But Werneth would not comment on the fate of the agency's outstanding positive outlook for James River ratings. The agency is working on an official comment, she said.
Moody's Investors Service did not return a phone call.
Some players had little optimism -- one trader who declined to be named said "someone's got to cut (James River). I don't know if it'll be Moody's or S&P, but somebody will."

Long maturity James River debt widened significantly from less than 100 basis points over Treasuries to a bid of 135 at mid-afternoon, however, reflecting investors concessions that the debt may be downgraded. Based on a positive outlook by S&P, the debt had been trading like an "upgrade candidate," an analyst said.
J.P. Morgan's Eadon said the debt would likely have widened further if investors were certain the credit would be downgraded.
Meanwhile, ten-year Fort Howard paper, rated B1/BB-minus, was boosted to a 135 basis point bid from 175 basis points.

James River and Fort Howard said on Monday they signed a definitive merger agreement to create a $7 billion paper and tissue products company to be called Fort James Corp. It is a stock for stock transaction in a deal valued at $5.8 billion, including the assumption of debt.
